title: Dark Mode Challenges
whyItMatters: A color chosen for a light background may lose its boundary on a dark surface, and extreme light-on-dark combinations can feel blurry.
learningObjectives: Understand why brand colors can fail on dark backgrounds.
Recognize the visual effect called halation.
Adapt colors for readability on dark surfaces.
lessonParagraphs: A light interface cannot always be converted to dark mode by simply reversing its colors. Brand colors designed for white backgrounds can lose contrast when placed on dark gray.
Dark mode may need a separate, less saturated version of brand colors. Dark text on a dark surface can also lose its boundary.
Halation describes the appearance of bright light bleeding into a dark area. The research discusses how pure white text on pure black can look fuzzy for people with astigmatism.
Off-white text on dark gray can soften the extremes and reduce glare while remaining above the stated minimum. Dark mode involves balancing measured contrast with visual comfort.

keyTakeaways: Colors designed for light backgrounds may not work on dark backgrounds.
Halation can make pure white text on pure black appear blurry.
Dark mode may need its own color palette.
reviewFlags: The source notes that perceptual algorithms handle dark-mode contrast differently and that the optimal levels remain debated.
